content: Accessible indoor routing is treated as a first-class routing mode, not a post-filter on the shortest path. Ariadne (Jul 2026) is the clearest statement: a step-free route prefers elevators and ramps over stairs and escalators, keeps within accessible grade and door-width limits, and every segment on the route must qualify, so a single unmarked step breaks the chain. The engine should compute the shortest path satisfying all constraints, remember the preference for the session, name the specific accessible elements it uses, and report honestly when no accessible path exists or the route is much longer. Mappedin (Mar 2026) adds verified WCAG 2.1 AA, step-free routing that auto-excludes stairs and escalators, screen-reader support and 40+ languages; MazeMap cites campuses shipping voice-guided navigation, high-contrast mode and wheelchair-friendly routing, and notes step-free routing is a legal obligation for universities.
